bansan.title: 晩餐
bansan.author: 素木しづ
bansan.blurb: A young couple feed their baby at supper while a storm blows outside, and one bad mouthful sends the mother somewhere far away.
bansan.about: Shiraki Shizu wrote this short sketch in 1917, the year before she died. A narrow room, a laughing child, a cold potato; and in a few lines the mother sees her three years of marriage as a whole long life, and a quiet peace waiting at the end of it.

shuchu.title: 酒虫
shuchu.author: 芥川龍之介
shuchu.blurb: A rich man who can drink all day and never get drunk lets a foreign monk tie him up in the summer sun, to draw out the worm in his belly that is doing the drinking.
shuchu.about: Akutagawa Ryūnosuke wrote this in 1916, retelling a tale from Pu Songling's Chinese collection Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio. He tells it with a straight face and a mock-scholarly air, and ends by offering three different answers to what the worm really was.

shokikan.title: 書記官
shokikan.author: 川上眉山
shokikan.blurb: At an autumn hot-spring inn, a rising young ministry secretary courts an old-fashioned man's daughter, and wins the father with a leaked draft of a cabinet order.
shokikan.about: Kawakami Bizan wrote this in 1895, one of the stories built around a social idea that made his name that year. He died in 1908.

rights.translation_search: No human English translation found (web, Meiji anthologies, English scholarship on Bizan's conceptual novels, 4 Nov 2026). The Japan Foundation database could not be reached that day.

yukigeshiki.title: 雪景色
yukigeshiki.author: 牧野信一
yukigeshiki.blurb: A writer who lives apart from his wife meets her at the family house, which is about to be pulled down, and she talks rings round him while two workmen fail to catch the carp in the pond.
yukigeshiki.about: Makino Shin'ichi published this in 1927. He was admired by the writers who came after him, Sakaguchi Ango among them, and died in 1936.

shiken.title: 死剣と生縄
shiken.author: 江見水蔭
shiken.blurb: A wandering swordsman kept as the 'guest' of a woman gang boss slips away to see his dying master, and falls in with a runaway acrobat girl and a brawling ex-monk.
shiken.about: Emi Suiin, a prolific writer of adventure and period stories, published this in a popular magazine in 1925. He died in 1934.

nekohachi.title: 猫八
nekohachi.author: 岩野泡鳴
nekohachi.blurb: Edoya Nekohachi, the comic famous for his animal cries, comes among a circle of writers, and the narrator sees what a lifetime of making people laugh has cost him.
nekohachi.about: Iwano Hōmei serialised this in the Osaka Mainichi newspaper in 1918, two years before he died. Its comic was a real performer, the first Edoya Nekohachi.
